page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v5 is an EASv5-series virtual machine configured with 48 vCPUs and 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, the instance features 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled and dedicated CPU allocation. The architecture is x86_64, supported by Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong CPU and memory performance. The instance ranks in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as PassMark CPU and memory scores. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and image processing also show strong performance. However, memory bandwidth for large blocks and database operations on PassMark fall into the average range. Large-scale LLM inference presents a notable bottleneck, with text generation for a 70B model scoring in the bottom 10% at 2.31 tokens per second, though smaller model text generation remains strong.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48as_v5 offers a high density of memory relative to compute resources without the added expense of local NVMe storage or GPU hardware. This makes it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that rely on network-attached storage. Appropriate workloads include memory-cached databases, enterprise applications, multi-threaded data decompression, and medium-scale analytical processing.
